transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-29 16:00 PST | Duration: 51 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Liu (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Delta CFO), Tom Rivera (Lead ML Engineer), Markus Engel (CTO)

Summary:
Short intake focused on unit economics across hosting options. Delta wants a clear break-even point: when does Dedicated/Private become cheaper than Redwood Hosted given their concurrency and latency targets. They surfaced budget ceilings, regulatory notes, and an experimentation window.

Topics: per-token pricing, batching & caching levers, burst capacity, SLA expectations, security/residency constraints, pilot scope

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick run-of-show — we'll walk through your traffic profile, show per-token examples, then Connor will sketch batching / kv cache impacts and we can map to hosted vs dedicated.
[00:22] Aisha: Thanks Maya. We're on a tight budget this Q, so main question is basically cost per event. We have a few patterns: chat assistant for checkout (short prompts), and an order-summary job that can be 2k to 4k tokens.
[00:40] Connor: Got it. Do you have approximate request per second or monthly tokens? even rough ranges help.
[00:50] Tom: Current pilots: ~350 qps peak for checkout, 18M tokens / month across features. Order-summary is ~120k jobs / month avg, each 2.5k tokens on average.
[01:12] Maya: Cool. So that mix means a heavy tail for longer sequences — that pushes dedicated GPU utilization higher if you need low-latency for summaries.
[01:30] Markus: We care about 250ms p95 for checkout responses and <2s for summaries. If latency for summaries is slightly higher we can batch, but checkout latency is non-negotiable.
[01:45] Connor: Right — that's a typical latency vs cost tradeoff. For checkout, hosted with low-latency routing and smaller model variants often works. For summaries, batching + KV cache and quantized models on Dedicated can reduce per-token cost by 40-60% depending on config.
[02:12] Aisha: When you say 40-60% is that versus hosted? and does that include reserved commitment costs?
[02:22] Maya: Good question. The delta depends — hosted per-token price is unit price plus our managed infra overhead. On Dedicated you amortize the GPU pool; so for sustained high volume, Dedicated per-token after amortization becomes lower. We'll show a break-even calc.
[02:40] Tom: Also curious about caching. If we cache KV/prefix for the checkout flows, does that actually reduce tokens billed or just latency?
[02:52] Connor: Two things: prefix/KV cache reduces compute by avoiding re-evaluating earlier context — it reduces billed tokens if you use prefix-embedding cache patterns or if you have repeated context. It also reduces latency because KV lookups are faster than recomputing. For Delta's checkout where prompts repeat a lot, that can be 20-35% reduction.
[03:15] Aisha: Hm. Our finance team wants to see a model: worst case hosted at X per month, best case Dedicated at Y per month with these caching assumptions.
[03:26] Maya: We'll deliver that. We'll model three scenarios: conservative (no cache, no quantization), realistic (moderate cache + batching), optimistic (aggressive quant + high cache hit).
[03:38] Markus: Security question — if we go Dedicated or Private, what's the difference in audit logs / SSO? we need SOC2 plus enterprise SSO.
[03:48] Maya: Dedicated has customer isolation at the pool level, plus SSO via SAML, RBAC, and audit logs with 90 day retention by default; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control of KMS and log routing. We'll attach our SOC 2 and ISO docs but for Private you'll likely want an on-prem package.
[04:12] Tom: Performance detail — our order-summary uses a 4k window for retrieval augmented generation, does Redwood support continuous KV with long context?
[04:23] Connor: Yes, the runtime supports KV caching and chunked context with optimized attention kernels. For long-RAG jobs, Dedicated with 80GB memory GPUs or our quantized variants helps. There are slight perf differences between kernels; we'll include a benchmark table.
[04:48] Aisha: Competitor check: we're also talking to OpenAI and AWS Bedrock. Their hosted numbers feel lower but the actual throughput tail and failover are uncertain. How do you compare?
[05:02] Maya: We try to be explicit: hosted is easy to start and predictable for bursty traffic. Our Published hosted prices include managed routing and fallback; Dedicated gives you SLO-backed latency and better unit cost for sustained workloads. Bedrock/OpenAI have their own tradeoffs around pricing transparency and private deployment.
[05:28] Markus: What about burst capacity? we have marketing spikes — can't drop checkout traffic.
[05:34] Connor: We offer autoscale + burst pools on Dedicated and hosted has multi-tenant excess capacity with some throttling. For critical checkout, we recommend canary routes to a higher-tier model or multi-region fallback. Those routing policies cost a bit more but keep availability high.
[05:55] Tom: Can you run a 24-hour pilot with our sample traces to show both cost and tail latency?
[06:02] Maya: Yes, that's exactly the suggestion — a short pilot mirroring your mix. We'll need a sanitized trace and API keys. Connor can run a config that simulates batching and KV caching.
[06:15] Aisha: Budget: FY Q1 we can allocate a $45k runway for initial pilot + evaluation; after that we need to justify committing to Dedicated. The finance folks want a clear payback period.
[06:28] Maya: We'll put together a payback model: months to breakeven for Dedicated at different sustained throughput levels. For example, at ~1.2M tokens/day sustained with your 2.5k summaries, Dedicated often becomes attractive. We'll show thresholds.
[06:46] Connor: Quick technical: batching window sizes matter. For lower-latency checkout we use continuous batching with tiny windows (30-50ms) — gives high throughput without much added latency. For summaries, you can batch up to 200ms or more and squeeze more tokens into GPU runs. Quantization also affects latency slightly but dramatically reduces memory and cost.
[07:10] Tom: Are there tradeoffs in output quality with quantized models?
[07:15] Connor: Slight differences, usually negligible for summarization. For creative chat, you'd want to test prompt-sensitive quality. We'll attach eval runs that show ROUGE/BLEU-ish deltas.
[07:32] Aisha: Let's talk numbers here; can you give rough hosted per-token rates for the models you'd recommend? even ballpark.
[07:40] Maya: Ballpark hosted text-gen model we showed in notebooks: $0.0009–$0.0015 per token depending on size; embeddings separate. On Dedicated after amortization could be $0.0004–$0.0009 per token for sustained use. We'll send a spreadsheet with scenarios.
[08:02] Markus: That delta could be meaningful. Our monthly tokens could scale to 80M if we push hard.
[08:09] Connor: Exactly — the more sustained volume, the more Dedicated wins. But if you have unpredictable bursts and low average, hosted reduces ops burden. Also routing policies let you mix: host checkout on hosted and route heavy summaries to Dedicated.
[08:29] Maya: Notes on chargebacks: we can show token-level breakdowns by route and model in Console so you can attribute cost to product teams.
[08:40] Aisha: Good. Also need to understand termination/binding — if we commit to Dedicated, what's minimum term and how flexible?
[08:49] Maya: Standard Dedicated is 12-month reserved with some burst allowances; we can discuss shorter pilots with credits. We'll outline options.
[09:02] Tom: For the pilot we'll supply sample traces and a subset of real prompts — any guardrails on PII?
[09:09] Maya: Send sanitized data; we can also run on Private or Dedicated with customer-controlled KMS if PII is a blocker.
[09:20] (brief cross talk)
[09:28] Connor: I'll take action to spin up a pilot config: 2 routes — low-latency hosted for checkout, a Dedicated pool for batched summaries. We'll simulate 24–48h under your traces and capture p50/p95/p99 and token costs.
[09:45] Aisha: That sounds good. Is there anything else from security perspective before we schedule the deep dive?
[09:51] Markus: We'll want to include our infosec: network rules, VPC peering, and KMS requirements.
[09:57] Maya: We'll arrange a security call. I'll send SOC2 and our Private deployment spec.
[10:06] Aisha: Perfect. I'm going to loop in procurement after we see the pilot numbers.

[10:18] Maya: Quick recap — next actions: Maya to send cost model and hosted/dedicated spreadsheet; Connor to run pilot with provided traces; schedule security deep dive next week.
[10:32] Aisha: Thanks — we'll get you the sanitized trace and confirm budget owner.
[10:38] Maya: Great, talk soon.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts mentioned: "Delta sample trace (sanitized)" link placeholder, Redwood SOC2/ISO link placeholder, dedicated vs hosted cost spreadsheet (will be shared).
